doc.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Will new tunes become standards?
summary: Bryant doubts modern modal tunes will become standards like 'Take the A Train'.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I’ve heard that tune done in so many ways, everything from marching bands and now a jazz trio. And I suppose we could say that it’s become a standard. And I’m always curious as to try to guess what tunes are being written now, or in the last ten or fifteen years, that will become standards, as most of our standards have come from the ‘40s, ‘30s. Are they being written now? New ones?

Well I don’t know. Some of the new things I heard are pretty — I guess they could be. But I listen to some of the new stuff and some it’s like shocking. Harmonically they’ve gone really, with the modal things and so forth, which I don’t really delve into. Some of them I like and some I’ll say well I don’t know. Interesting, things that they’re doing these days. I don’t know how long lasting they may end up being, that just remains to be seen. But we’re not going to see to many “Take the A Train”’s or “C Jam Blues” I don’t think so.
